title: Identifier cannot be changed after creation
gherkin:
Given an entity with an identifier
When I attempt to modify the identifier
Then the identifier should remain unchanged
And the system should reject the modification
rationale: Core immutability requirement - identifiers must not be modifiable after initial creation to maintain data integrity and consistency.
generationSummary: Test cases for identifier immutability rule - verifying that identifiers cannot be modified once created and remain constant throughout the system lifecycle.

title: Identifier persists across system operations
gherkin:
Given an entity with an assigned identifier
When the entity undergoes various operations
Then the identifier should remain constant throughout all operations
And the identifier should be retrievable in its original form
rationale: Identifiers must maintain their value across all system operations to ensure consistent entity tracking and reference.
generationSummary: Test cases for identifier immutability rule - verifying that identifiers cannot be modified once created and remain constant throughout the system lifecycle.

title: Identifier cannot be deleted
gherkin:
Given an entity with an identifier
When I attempt to delete the identifier
Then the deletion should fail
And the identifier should still exist on the entity
rationale: Immutability includes protection against deletion - identifiers must persist for the lifetime of the entity.
generationSummary: Test cases for identifier immutability rule - verifying that identifiers cannot be modified once created and remain constant throughout the system lifecycle.

rationale: Immutability ensures identifiers remain uniquely bound to their original entities and cannot be reassigned.
